claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi is governed partly by its intrinsic magnetic transition.
The density and distribution of grain boundaries, internal strain, and defects govern the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of the FeMnNiGeSi alloy.
The relevant grain boundaries, strain fields, and defects are inherited from rapid solidification.
Microstructural heterogeneities pin the magnetostructural transition.
Pinning by these heterogeneities causes a sharp first-order transition with significant hysteretic energy loss.
Changes in structural parameters can alter magnetic exchange interactions and thereby affect magnetocaloric behavior.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy has a single-phase ordered hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with significant hysteresis.
The baseline alloy has limited heat-exchange performance because of its low surface-to-volume ratio.
Rapid thermal annealing or surface nanostructuring can selectively modify the near-surface microstructure without changing bulk composition or mechanical stability.
The proposed treatment will refine the grain size and relax internal strains.
Near-surface modification will reduce heterogeneous nucleation barriers and transition pinning.
Reduced nucleation barriers and pinning will produce a more diffuse magnetostructural transition.
A more diffuse transition will reduce magnetic and thermal hysteresis losses.
Increasing effective surface area through the treatment will improve the heat-exchange rate.
The treated alloy will exhibit a broader temperature range of entropy change and a lower peak entropy-change value than the as-deposited baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit lower hysteresis loss than the as-deposited baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit a faster thermal response than the as-deposited baseline.
The predictions are intended to apply near room temperature under applied fields of no more than 1 T.
